utterances.text: This is an accurate reflection of what the United Nations and the international observers and the NGOs are reporting up their chain. So in this particular context, they are accurately reporting the information they are receiving.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. May I tender that, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P4936, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I have 65 ter 09130, please, 09130. This is a -- still continuing to talk about MUP reporting on 12 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is at your tab 59 in the first binder, back to the first binder, Mr. Butler. It's again to the RS MUP, Bijeljina police forces staff from Chief Vasic. "We notify you that the evacuation and transportation of the civilian population from Srebrenica is underway." Then it begins to talk about the majority of men of military age, about 8.000, of whom 1.500 armed, led by Ejub Golic and Ibrahim Mandzic are in the Konjevic Polje and Sandici sector, the Sekovici Special Detachment, the 1st Company of the PJP, the same units we were talking about earlier, and the 5th Company of the Zvornik CJB are blocking this section with the goal of destroying these forces. [As read] "For the above reasons I've ordered the roads, Drinjaca," et cetera, "and am hereby notifying you we obtained all the above information from the four men we captured in Konjevic Polje an hour ago at about 1630 hours." So this report's at approximately 1730, around the time of Vujadin Popovic's report. Can you comment now about, first of all, again the efficacy of the reporting chain through the MUP about military developments on the field?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER
utterances.text: Yes, sir. And in fact, there are corresponding military reports discussing this same topic from these same four prisoners. So the MUP and the army people at least within the security and intelligence organs are talking to each other to ensure that information is being shared. And again going back to my earlier discussion on the legitimate purpose why the RDB and the state security organs and the military security organs would want to be interviewing people, it is precisely to identify relevant, pertinent combat-related information to gain an understanding of what the enemy is doing in the immediate future so you can react to it. So this is an excellent example of that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And my second question is: What this document, from your knowledge and your study, tells us about the role of the MUP where Vasic speaks about -- that the various MUP forces, Sekovici Specials, 1st Company PJP from Zvornik, et cetera, are now going to engage in blocking the road knowing about this group of Muslim men who were trying to break through.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER
utterances.text: Yes, sir. And in fact, later on the day of 12 July, those units, those police units that were in Potocari were ordered or most of them were ordered to be withdrawn from Potocari and redeployed along the Konjevic Polje-Kravica-Bratunac road because the army recognised that there were inadequate forces along that particular area to prevent the column from breaking through. So we know that that in fact occurred. So Vasic is again giving an accurate report as to what is happening with the situation on the ground and what the orders of the various police units are in relation to the growing military threat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls, we'll admit this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. I think I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And this maybe a proper moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be admitted as Exhibit P4937. Yes. We'll stop here. And if you could excuse yourself, Mr. Butler, I'll see you tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll resume tomorrow at 9.00. Yes. Shall we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Before we do, Mr. President, there's one quick matter I can raise in public session. That is with respect to the Registrar's filing of the time estimates. We wouldn't be disputing that, so perhaps it's unnecessary to submit anything in writing and this acknowledgement can take care of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes. Now could the Chamber move into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Hearing is adjourned for today and will resume tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
